The amendment would have struck a feasibility study for creating a Center of Excellence in Ukraine, but it failed to pass.
The Gaetz amendment to H.R. 2670 sought to prohibit all security assistance for Ukraine under the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative.
An amendment to strike $300 million in foreign military aid for Ukraine and eliminate land-lease authority for the country.
Resolution directing the President to remove all United States Armed Forces, except those protecting the U.S. Embassy, from Somalia.
The resolution directed the President to withdraw U.S. armed forces from Syria under the War Powers Resolution.

The amendment would reduce the sunset provision for Section 5112(c) of the Department of State Authorization Act from two years to one year, shortening the period of U.S. security assistance authority to Ukraine.

Amendment prohibits the President from selling or exporting new F‑16s or upgrade kits to Turkey unless a certification to Congress confirms the transfer is in U.S. national interest and includes safeguards against unauthorized overflights of Greece.
Amendment to prohibit U.S. military presence in Syria without Congressional approval within one year of enactment.

The amendment sought to cut the National Defense Authorization Act for FY2023 by $100 billion, reducing the overall authorized defense spending without changing personnel, civilian pay, benefits, or the Defense Health Program.
Provided $5.5 billion in additional military aid to Ukraine.
The House passed a resolution to agree to consider the Additional Ukraine Supplemental Appropriations Act, which would provide additional U.S. aid to Ukraine.
The Stop Iranian Drones Act, passed by the House, bans U.S. assistance and export of drone technology to Iran to curb its drone program.
The Asset Seizure for Ukraine Reconstruction Act authorized the use of seized Russian assets to fund reconstruction assistance for Ukraine.
Passed the Suspending Energy Imports from Russia Act, which imposed a ban on the importation of Russian oil, natural gas, and coal into the United States as a non-military economic sanction.
The House agreed to an amendment requiring the suspension of U.S. sustainment and maintenance support to Saudi Air Force units involved in airstrikes causing civilian casualties in Yemen.

The House agreed to an amendment to H.R. 4350 that terminates U.S. military logistical support, spare parts transfers, and coordination efforts for Saudi and UAE-led coalition forces conducting strikes in Yemen.
The House voted down an amendment that would have prohibited the U.S. military presence in Syria without Congressional approval within one year of the bill's enactment.
Passed the Department of State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs Appropriations Act for FY2022, which funds foreign aid and military assistance programs globally.
The House voted to repeal the 2002 Authorization for Use of Military Force Against Iraq, removing the legal authority for U.S. military operations in that country.

BG:R000610.description: Guy Lorin Reschenthaler is an American politician, attorney, judge, and U.S. Navy veteran. A Republican, he is serving as the U.S. representative for Pennsylvania's 14th congressional district since 2019 and was previously a member of the Pennsylvania State Senate, representing the 37th district. He served as a district judge, and in the U.S. Navy Judge Advocate General's Corps (JAG) during the Iraq War. He is serving as the Republican chief deputy whip in the 119th Congress.

BG:T000480.description: William Richardson Timmons IV is an American politician, prosecutor, and Air Force officer serving as the U.S. representative for South Carolina's 4th congressional district since 2019. He is a member of the Republican Party.

BG:N000190.description: Ralph Warren Norman Jr. is an American politician and real estate developer who has served as the U.S. representative for South Carolina's 5th congressional district since 2017. His district includes most of the South Carolina side of the Charlotte metropolitan area, along with outer portions of the Upstate and Midlands. Norman's tenure in Congress will end in January 2027 after unsuccessful gubernatorial and U.S. Senate bids.

BG:J000301.description: Dustin Michael Johnson is an American politician serving as the U.S. representative for South Dakota's at-large congressional district since 2019. A member of the Republican Party, he served as South Dakota Public Utilities Commissioner from 2005 to 2011, when he was appointed chief of staff to Governor Dennis Daugaard, a position he held until 2014. Between his state political career and congressional service, Johnson was the vice-president of Vantage Point Solutions in Mitchell, South Dakota.

BG:K000392.description: David Frank Kustoff is an American politician and attorney serving as the United States representative from Tennessee's 8th congressional district. The district includes the bulk of West Tennessee, but most of its population is in the eastern part of the Memphis area, including the eastern fourth of Memphis itself. From 2006 to 2008, Kustoff served as a United States attorney for the Western District of Tennessee. He is one of four Jewish Republicans in Congress, alongside Max Miller, Randy Fine, and Craig Goldman.

Provided $5.5 billion in additional military aid to Ukraine.

The House voted down an amendment that would have prohibited the U.S. military presence in Syria without Congressional approval within one year of the bill's enactment.
Passed the Department of State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs Appropriations Act for FY2022, which funds foreign aid and military assistance programs globally.
The House voted to repeal the 2002 Authorization for Use of Military Force Against Iraq, removing the legal authority for U.S. military operations in that country.
The House voted on a motion to recommit H.R. 256, which sought to repeal the 2002 Authorization for Use of Military Force Against Iraq, effectively blocking the repeal of the war authorization.

BG:C001063.description: Enrique Roberto "Henry" Cuellar is an American politician and attorney serving as the U.S. representative for Texas's 28th congressional district since 2005. He is a member of the Democratic Party, and his district spans from the Rio Grande toward the suburbs of San Antonio. Cuellar served in the Texas House of Representatives for 14 years, from 1987 to 2001, and briefly served as the Texas secretary of state in 2001, making him, as of 2026, the most recent Democrat to have held a statewide office in Texas.

BG:C001131.description: Gregorio Eduardo Casar is an American politician serving as a U.S. representative from Texas's 35th congressional district since 2023. He served as a member of the Austin City Council from the 4th district from 2015 to 2022. Casar is a member of the Democratic Party and was endorsed by the Working Families Party in his run for Congress. He was first elected to the Austin City Council in 2014, representing District 4. He was reelected in 2016 and 2020. He was elected to Congress in 2022.

BG:M001227.description: Jennifer Leigh McClellan is an American politician and attorney who has served as the U.S. representative for Virginia's 4th congressional district since 2023. A member of the Democratic Party, she represented the 9th district in the Virginia State Senate from 2017 to 2023 and the 71st district in the Virginia House of Delegates from 2006 to 2017. She ran in the Democratic primary for governor of Virginia in the 2021 election, losing to former governor Terry McAuliffe.

vote_record.summary: Passed a concurrent resolution directing the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran pursuant to the War Powers Resolution.
The House passed a concurrent resolution directing the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran pursuant to the War Powers Resolution.
The amendment would prohibit all U.S. security assistance to Ukraine except for U.S. embassy security, effectively cutting aid to Ukraine.

The amendment would prohibit the Department of Defense from using taxpayer funds to cover the costs of foreign military personnel participating in bilateral or multilateral exercises unless the Secretary of Defense waives the prohibition.
On Agreeing to the Amendment - H.R. 8595 - Amends the Foreign Military Financing Program and the National Security Investment Programs to reduce funding for Jordan by $2,100,000,000. Failed.

On Agreeing to the Amendment - H.R. 8595 - H.Amdt. 8: Amendment sought to prohibit funds appropriated by the Act from being used for Israel, and accordingly reduces the Foreign Military Financing Program account by $3,300,000,000. Failed.
House passes a resolution to remove U.S. forces from hostilities in Lebanon, passing 193-218 with 187 Democrats, 2 Independents, and 2 Republicans voting in favor.
The Ukraine Support Act authorized additional U.S. military and economic assistance for Ukraine.
The House voted to agree to H. CON. RES. 84, which would direct the President to remove U.S. armed forces from Lebanon under the War Powers Resolution; the motion failed.
The resolution directed the President to withdraw U.S. armed forces from hostilities with Iran under the War Powers Resolution.
The resolution directed the President to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities against Iran under the War Powers Resolution.
The resolution directed the President to remove United States armed forces from hostilities with Iran under the War Powers Resolution.
The resolution directed the President to withdraw U.S. armed forces from unauthorized hostilities in Iran.
The PROTECT Taiwan Act passed, directing the administration to strengthen U.S. security assistance and consider additional defensive arms sales to Taiwan.
The resolution would have directed the withdrawal of U.S. armed forces from Venezuela, but it failed to pass.
The resolution directed the removal of United States armed forces from hostilities in or against Venezuela that were not authorized by Congress.
The resolution directed the President to withdraw U.S. armed forces from hostilities with presidentially designated terrorist organizations in the Western Hemisphere.
An amendment to strike funding for the Taiwan Security Cooperation Initiative was defeated, with 9 yeas and 213 nays.
An amendment to H.R. 3838 proposed prohibiting U.S. assistance to Ukraine, but it failed with 60 yeas and 372 nays.
The amendment repealed the 1991 and 2002 Authorizations for Use of Military Force, ending those authorizations.
The amendment would have prohibited all U.S. assistance to the Lebanese Armed Forces, but it failed with 76 yeas and 212 nays.
The amendment would have stripped funding for U.S. assistance to Ukraine.
The amendment sought to strike funding for U.S. military assistance to Jordan.
An amendment to cut funding for the Israeli Cooperative Programs was proposed but failed, preserving the existing aid.
The amendment sought to strike funding for the Taiwan Security Cooperation Initiative, but it failed.
The House passed H.R. 8771, appropriating funds for the Department of State, foreign operations, and related programs for fiscal year 2025.
Amendment to prohibit the use of funds in the bill for acquiring, using, transferring, or selling cluster munitions.
The amendment sought to prohibit U.S. funding for Ukraine, but it failed.
Amendment prohibits any foreign assistance funds in the bill from being made available to areas of Syria controlled by Bashar al-Assad, both directly and indirectly.
The amendment prohibited the use of funds from the Act to support the Gaza pier, effectively blocking U.S. assistance to Hamas’s military infrastructure.
The amendment sought to prohibit U.S. funds to the Lebanese Armed Forces, but it failed.
The amendment sought to prohibit U.S. funding for the United Nations unless specifically authorized by Congress, effectively restricting U.S. financial support to the UN.
The amendment bars the use of funds to administer or enforce the National Security Memorandum on safeguards and accountability for transferred defense articles and services.
The amendment sought to prohibit U.S. funding for the International Organization for Migration's activities in the Western Hemisphere.
Amendment to prohibit U.S. funding for Ukraine.
The amendment sought to prohibit funding for the Special Representative for Ukraine's Economic Recovery, cutting U.S. aid to Ukraine.
The amendment sought to prohibit funding for the Bilateral Security Agreement between the United States and Ukraine.
The amendment sought to prohibit funding for foreign military sales to Ukraine, but it failed.
The amendment sought to prohibit the transfer of cluster munitions, but it failed to pass.
The amendment prohibited any use of the Act’s funds for assistance to Ukraine.
Amendment to bar the use of funds for any NATO‑related project or activity until each member country has spent 2% of its GDP on defense; the amendment failed.
The House voted down an amendment to strike funding for the North Atlantic Treaty Organization Security Investment Program.
Passed the Israel Security Assistance Support Act, which authorizes additional military aid and security assistance for Israel.
The House voted to reject a motion to recommit the Israel Security Assistance Support Act, which would have authorized $14 billion in military aid to Israel.
Passed the Israel Security Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2024, providing $14.3 billion in military aid to Israel.
Passed the Ukraine Security Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2024, providing approximately $61 billion in security assistance to Ukraine.

The House voted on a motion to recommit the Ukraine Security Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2024, which would have provided $61 billion in security assistance to Ukraine; the motion failed, allowing the bill to proceed.
The House rejected an amendment that would have struck provisions increasing the President's authority to draw down and transfer defense articles to foreign countries.
The House passed the Standing Against Houthi Aggression Act, authorizing the use of military force against the Houthi group in Yemen to protect U.S. personnel and shipping.
Passed the No U.S. Financing for Iran Act, which prohibits the use of U.S. government funds to finance the purchase of Iranian goods or services.
The House voted down a motion to suspend the rules and pass the Israel Security Supplemental Appropriations Act, which would have provided additional military aid and security funding to Israel.
Passed the No Funds for Iranian Terrorism Act, which prohibits the use of U.S. funds for the transfer of military equipment, training, or assistance to the Government of Iran.
The House agreed to an amendment prohibiting the President from waiving statutory restrictions on arms sales to Iran, thereby blocking potential executive discretion to approve such transfers.

Passed the Hamas and Other Palestinian Terrorist Groups International Financing Prevention Act to prohibit U.S. financial assistance to entities designated as terrorist organizations, including Hamas.

Passed the Department of State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2024, which funds foreign aid and military assistance programs for various countries including Israel and Ukraine.
The House rejected an amendment to reduce foreign assistance to countries based on the number of unaccompanied alien children entering the U.S. from those nations.
The House rejected an amendment that would have prohibited the use of funds from the bill to transfer cluster munitions to any foreign country.
The House voted down an amendment that would have prohibited the use of funds in the bill for Pakistan.
The House voted down an amendment to the FY2024 State Department and Foreign Operations Appropriations Act that would have prohibited the use of funds to provide assistance to Iraq.
The House rejected an amendment to prohibit the use of funds for the Lebanese Armed Forces.
The House voted down an amendment that would have prohibited the use of funds to initiate a drawdown and delivery of defense articles and services from Department of Defense stocks to Ukraine.
The House voted down an amendment to prohibit assistance to Ukraine, thereby allowing the aid to proceed.
The House rejected an amendment to reduce Economic Support Fund funding for Egypt and Jordan to FY2018 levels.
The House rejected an amendment to prohibit the use of funds from the bill to transfer cluster munitions.
The House voted down an amendment by Rep. Matt Gaetz that would have prohibited the provision of security assistance to Ukraine.
The vote rejected an amendment to reduce funding for the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative by $300 million.
The House rejected an amendment to reduce the NATO Security Investment Program account by $73,334,000.
The House rejected an amendment to reduce the NATO Security Investment Program by $3 million.
The House agreed to an amendment prohibiting the Department of Defense from providing any support to the Taliban and banning sanctions relief for Afghanistan unless explicitly authorized by Congress.

The House rejected an amendment to strike Section 217 of H.R. 2670, which would have removed authorization for funds to the NATO Defence Innovation Accelerator for the North Atlantic (DIANA) initiative.
The House rejected an amendment that would have prohibited the sale or transfer of cluster munitions to Ukraine.
The vote failed to adopt an amendment that would have struck the provision extending lend-lease authority to Ukraine, thereby preserving the authority to provide military aid to Ukraine.
The amendment would have struck a feasibility study for creating a Center of Excellence in Ukraine, but it failed to pass.
The Gaetz amendment to H.R. 2670 sought to prohibit all security assistance for Ukraine under the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative.
An amendment to strike $300 million in foreign military aid for Ukraine and eliminate land-lease authority for the country.
Resolution directing the President to remove all United States Armed Forces, except those protecting the U.S. Embassy, from Somalia.
The resolution directed the President to withdraw U.S. armed forces from Syria under the War Powers Resolution.

The amendment would reduce the sunset provision for Section 5112(c) of the Department of State Authorization Act from two years to one year, shortening the period of U.S. security assistance authority to Ukraine.

Amendment prohibits the President from selling or exporting new F‑16s or upgrade kits to Turkey unless a certification to Congress confirms the transfer is in U.S. national interest and includes safeguards against unauthorized overflights of Greece.
Amendment to prohibit U.S. military presence in Syria without Congressional approval within one year of enactment.

The amendment sought to cut the National Defense Authorization Act for FY2023 by $100 billion, reducing the overall authorized defense spending without changing personnel, civilian pay, benefits, or the Defense Health Program.
Provided $5.5 billion in additional military aid to Ukraine.
The House passed a resolution to agree to consider the Additional Ukraine Supplemental Appropriations Act, which would provide additional U.S. aid to Ukraine.
The Stop Iranian Drones Act, passed by the House, bans U.S. assistance and export of drone technology to Iran to curb its drone program.
The Asset Seizure for Ukraine Reconstruction Act authorized the use of seized Russian assets to fund reconstruction assistance for Ukraine.
Passed the Suspending Energy Imports from Russia Act, which imposed a ban on the importation of Russian oil, natural gas, and coal into the United States as a non-military economic sanction.
The House agreed to an amendment requiring the suspension of U.S. sustainment and maintenance support to Saudi Air Force units involved in airstrikes causing civilian casualties in Yemen.

The House agreed to an amendment to H.R. 4350 that terminates U.S. military logistical support, spare parts transfers, and coordination efforts for Saudi and UAE-led coalition forces conducting strikes in Yemen.
The House voted down an amendment that would have prohibited the U.S. military presence in Syria without Congressional approval within one year of the bill's enactment.
Passed the Department of State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs Appropriations Act for FY2022, which funds foreign aid and military assistance programs globally.
The House voted to repeal the 2002 Authorization for Use of Military Force Against Iraq, removing the legal authority for U.S. military operations in that country.
The House voted on a motion to recommit H.R. 256, which sought to repeal the 2002 Authorization for Use of Military Force Against Iraq, effectively blocking the repeal of the war authorization.

Passed the Suspending Energy Imports from Russia Act, which imposed a ban on the importation of Russian oil, natural gas, and coal into the United States as a non-military economic sanction.
The House agreed to an amendment requiring the suspension of U.S. sustainment and maintenance support to Saudi Air Force units involved in airstrikes causing civilian casualties in Yemen.

The House voted down an amendment that would have prohibited the U.S. military presence in Syria without Congressional approval within one year of the bill's enactment.
Passed the Department of State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs Appropriations Act for FY2022, which funds foreign aid and military assistance programs globally.
The House voted to repeal the 2002 Authorization for Use of Military Force Against Iraq, removing the legal authority for U.S. military operations in that country.

BG:N000189.description: Daniel Milton Newhouse is an American politician serving as the U.S. representative for Washington's 4th congressional district. The district covers much of the central third of the state, including Yakima and the Tri-Cities. Before his election to Congress, Newhouse served as director of the Washington State Department of Agriculture and as a member of the Washington House of Representatives. He is a member of the Republican Party.

BG:J000298.description: Pramila Jayapal is an American politician serving as the U.S. representative from Washington's 7th congressional district since 2017. A member of the Democratic Party, she represents most of Seattle, as well as some suburban areas of King County. Jayapal represented the 37th legislative district in the Washington State Senate from 2015 to 2017. She is the first Indian American woman to serve in the U.S. House of Representatives. The district's first female member of Congress, she is also the first Asian American to represent Washington at the federal level.

The district is based in the state capital of Olympia, and also includes much of eastern Tacoma. A member of the Democratic Party, Strickland took office on January 3, 2021. She previously served as the 38th mayor of Tacoma from 2010 to 2018.

The House rejected an amendment that would have prohibited the sale or transfer of cluster munitions to Ukraine.

Amendment prohibits the President from selling or exporting new F‑16s or upgrade kits to Turkey unless a certification to Congress confirms the transfer is in U.S. national interest and includes safeguards against unauthorized overflights of Greece.
Amendment to prohibit U.S. military presence in Syria without Congressional approval within one year of enactment.

The Asset Seizure for Ukraine Reconstruction Act authorized the use of seized Russian assets to fund reconstruction assistance for Ukraine.
Passed the Suspending Energy Imports from Russia Act, which imposed a ban on the importation of Russian oil, natural gas, and coal into the United States as a non-military economic sanction.
The House agreed to an amendment requiring the suspension of U.S. sustainment and maintenance support to Saudi Air Force units involved in airstrikes causing civilian casualties in Yemen.

The House agreed to an amendment to H.R. 4350 that terminates U.S. military logistical support, spare parts transfers, and coordination efforts for Saudi and UAE-led coalition forces conducting strikes in Yemen.
The House voted down an amendment that would have prohibited the U.S. military presence in Syria without Congressional approval within one year of the bill's enactment.
Passed the Department of State, Foreign Operations, and Related Programs Appropriations Act for FY2022, which funds foreign aid and military assistance programs globally.
The House voted to repeal the 2002 Authorization for Use of Military Force Against Iraq, removing the legal authority for U.S. military operations in that country.
The House voted on a motion to recommit H.R. 256, which sought to repeal the 2002 Authorization for Use of Military Force Against Iraq, effectively blocking the repeal of the war authorization.

BG:S001213.description: Bryan George Steil is an American attorney, businessman, and Republican politician from Janesville, Wisconsin. He is a member of the United States House of Representatives, representing Wisconsin's 1st congressional district since 2019. Since 2023, he has served as chair of the House Administration Committee. Prior to his election to Congress, he served on the University of Wisconsin Board of Regents.
